$comment: Example GENESIS mod pack — a chronicle set: 'The Book of Ash', a darker, older voice for the chronicle (CONTRACT §13). Templates are matched by id (events.json): an id the base pack has is RE-VOICED in place, a new id is added (the sim tells the most specific id it finds: 'discovery.accident.lightning-dune' before 'discovery.accident'). Because it changes existing templates, load it before the world is made (the worker's {type:'mod'} message before 'init', or Sim({ content: [pack] })); a running world only takes packs that add new things.
name: The Book of Ash

text: Here the {people} put down their stones and named the place {settlement}. Count the years from this.
{count} of the {people} stopped walking. The place they stopped became {settlement}.
{agent} of {settlement} burned their fingers and spoiled their work a hundred times, and then it held: {knowledge}.
Nobody taught {agent} of {settlement}. The failures taught {pron}: {knowledge}.
{agent} of {settlement} was buried with {knowledge} still in {pron2} hands. Nobody had asked. It is gone.
The earth took {agent} of {settlement}, and {knowledge} with {pron}. Write things down.
{settlement} is a name on a stone now ({cause}).
The roofs of {settlement} fell in and the {people} did not come back to mend them ({cause}).
{disease} came to {settlement} like a guest who would not leave.
In {settlement} they began to dig graves before the dying had stopped breathing: {disease}.
{planet} keeps its rivers and its weather and nobody to see them. The people are gone.
The {ship} {name} of {settlement} climbed on a column of fire until it was a star among stars: the first of {home} to leave it.
For the first time, the ground of {home} let one of its children go: the {ship} {name}, {count} aboard.
The {people} of {settlement} had thought they were alone under the sky. Then {others} came down from it, out of {home}.
Two worlds that had watched each other as lights met at {settlement}: the {people}, and {others} from {home}.
Somewhere between {home} and {planet} the {ship} {name} went quiet ({cause}). The dark keeps {count} of the {people} of {settlement}.
The {people} of {settlement} knelt in the scorched ring where the visitors' ship had stood, and called them {god}.
Strangers came, and left something behind besides their footprints: {agent} of {settlement} learned {knowledge} from them.
The war taught {settlement} what peace never had: {agent} learned {knowledge} among the dead.
Through polished glass the {people} of {settlement} saw {planet} clearly for the first time: {desc}. They were less alone than they had thought.
